mcp.note: REAL, not a scaffold — this repo SHIPS an MCP bridge (one surface of the product, not its whole identity — see portal.reason): a Figma plugin (manifest.json, editorType figma/figjam) talking to a localhost MCP server over bridge-server.js. Outstanding for mcp-maintainer: (1) fuzex-figma-bridge still has no tools.json declaring its surface or `mutates` per tool — the plugin protocol in code.js handles start-server/stop-server/mcp-request/client-connect/client-disconnect/get-server-status/ping, which is transport, not a tool manifest; (2) mcp-server-config.json hardcodes an absolute Windows cwd (C:/Users/izzyw/source/FuzeX) so the config is not portable to any other machine or to CI. The second server, design-frames-service, DOES declare tools.json with `mutates` per tool (services/design-frames-service/mcp/tools.json) — added together with the service in the navigable-frames extraction; see services/design-frames-service/docs/EXTRACTION.md.

portal.reason: FuzeX registers itself. CORRECTION (2026-08-19) — this note previously said it did not: that FuzeX was a Figma/FigJam plugin rather than a web app, that its UI ran in Figma's plugin sandbox with networkAccess restricted to localhost, that there was therefore no served origin to iframe and no remoteEntry to federate, and that registration in the app-registry manifest was handled by an orchestrator rather than by this repo. Every one of those clauses is now false, and they are recorded here rather than deleted because the change was a deliberate evolution, not a contradiction: FuzeX grew from a static, local frame-approval tool into a full SaaS product for UX/UI management, and it is now a product like every other one in the family. What it has today: a served backend (services/design-frames-service — REST + MCP + A2A, GET /health and GET /openapi answered ahead of any auth), a served frontend on that same real origin calling its API on a same-origin base path, a Module-Federation remote (services/design-frames-service/webapp — scope `fuzex`, module `./DesignFramesApp`, built into the service image and served BY THIS SERVICE at /apps/fuzex/remoteEntry.js, sharing the host's React 19 singleton at requiredVersion ^19.0.0), its own Helm chart with an UNCONDITIONAL, fail-closed registration init container (deploy/helm/fuzex), its own registration payload (registration/manifest.json + registration/policy.json, slug `fuzex` with display name `X` — the prefix comes off the NAME, not the slug, and for FuzeX the slug must keep it: `x` is one character, below the contract's 3-character Slug minimum, so it would 400 and CrashLoopBackOff the pod), and its own Argo CD Application (deploy/argocd/application.yaml). Registration belongs to this repo and to no orchestrator. The Figma/FigJam plugin (manifest.json, code.js, ui.html) still exists as ONE surface of the product and still runs sandboxed with localhost-only network access — that part was always true and remains true. It is simply no longer the whole of what FuzeX is.
